claim: 早期佛教教说保存于尼柯耶/阿含，主题是从苦中解脱；SEP 将佛陀作为哲学家处理、对其超人间属性存而不论。
locator: SEP Buddha 开篇：'The Buddha (fl. circa 450 BCE) is the individual whose teachings form the basis of the Buddhist tradition.'；'These teachings, preserved in texts known as the Nikāyas or Āgamas, concern the quest for liberation from suffering.'；'The Buddha will here be treated as a philosopher.'；'taking an agnostic stance on the question of whether there have been other buddhas'
note: 'fl. circa 450 BCE' 为本包独立提取（T01 未用此句）。

claim: 证据三重困难：文本迟至身后数世纪书面化、语言非佛陀本人可能说的语言、各文本互不一致。
locator: SEP Buddha：'Our knowledge of the Buddha's teachings comes by way of texts that were not written down until several centuries after his death, are in languages (Pāli, and Chinese translations of Sanskrit) other than the one he is likely to have spoken, and disagree in important respects.'

claim: 现存诸藏全部已部派化；任何重构都是尝试性的。
locator: Wikipedia Pre-sectarian Buddhism：'Earliest Buddhism can only be deduced from the various Buddhist canons now extant, which are all already sectarian collections.'；'As such any reconstruction is tentative.'
note: 本包 overview 方法论原则的直接根据。

claim: 佛陀年代两说：旧说约前560—480，今多数学者主必死于约前405；约活动于前450年前后。
locator: SEP Buddha：'Up until recently his dates were thought to be approximately 560–480 BCE, but many scholars now hold that he must have died around 405 BCE.'；'The Buddha (fl. circa 450 BCE)'
note: 站内纪年'约前5世纪（具体生卒年有争议）'与之相容，已并陈。
uncertainty: 年代两说并存，不采单一说。

claim: 四圣谛框架及四句内容。
locator: SEP Buddha：'The Buddha's basic teachings are usually summarized using the device of the Four Nobles' Truths: There is suffering. There is the origination of suffering. There is the cessation of suffering. There is a path to the cessation of suffering.'
note: SEP 原文作 'Four Nobles' Truths'（复数所有格），引文保持原样。

claim: 见四谛即证知终极真理（SEP 引 Gethin）。
locator: SEP Abhidharma（引 Gethin，脚注9）：'And in seeing these four truths one realizes the ultimate truth— dhamma —about the world.'
note: 这是 SEP 条目内的引语，已在 packet 中标为'SEP 引 Gethin'。

claim: SN 56.11 以二边/中道开篇并列出八正道八支；四谛随后宣说。
locator: Access to Insight SN 56.11（Thanissaro 英译）：'Avoiding both of these extremes, the middle way realized by the Tathagata — producing vision, producing knowledge — leads to calm, to direct knowledge, to self-awakening, to Unbinding.'；'Precisely this Noble Eightfold Path: right view, right resolve, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right concentration.'
note: 结构观察为本包对读所得，两个 verbatim 句均逐字核自页面。

claim: 汉译 SA 379 无中道开篇，直接以'此苦聖諦'进入，并含'三轉十二行'教法展开。
locator: 维基文库《雜阿含經》卷15 三七九经逐字：'如是我聞：' 后接 '一時，佛住波羅㮈鹿野苑中仙人住處。'；'爾時，世尊告五比丘：「此苦聖諦，本所未曾聞法，當正思惟。時，生眼、智、明、覺'；'我已於四聖諦三轉十二行生眼、智、明、覺'
note: '无中道开篇'为本包对该页全文的对读观察（已通读三七九经全段），非转引。
uncertainty: 该差异的文献学解释（孰早孰晚）属 S3/S5 所载争论，本包不断定。

claim: 苦的分析落在五取蕴，集的分析落在渴爱三向，灭谛是渴爱的无余灭尽。
locator: Access to Insight SN 56.11：'In short, the five clinging-aggregates are stressful.'；'the craving that makes for further becoming — accompanied by passion & delight, relishing now here & now there — i.e., craving for sensual pleasure, craving for becoming, craving for non-becoming.'；'the remainderless fading & cessation, renunciation, relinquishment, release, & letting go of that very craving.'

claim: 缘起十二支及'较晚编纂'的文献学警示：文本给出两个略异版本、存在更短表述。
locator: SEP Buddha：'a list consisting of twelve links in a causal chain that begins with ignorance and ends with suffering (represented by the states of old age, disease and death)'；'Modern scholarship has established that this list is a later compilation.'；'For the texts that claim to convey the Buddha's own teachings give two slightly different formulations of this list, and shorter formulations containing only some of the twelve items are also found in the texts.'
note: 该警示是本包'按来源呈现分层'写法的直接支柱。

claim: 无我论证的重构（无常论证）与'我/我的之慢'。
locator: SEP Buddha：'the conceit that there is an ‘I’ and a ‘mine’. This is the famous Buddhist teaching of non-self (anātman).'；'1. If there were a self it would be permanent. 2. None of the five kinds of psychophysical element is permanent. ∴ There is no self.'（S III.66–8 出处标注见同段；内层引号字形从原文）

claim: 无我诠释之争：有解释者谓佛陀未断然否认超越经验所给的自我；古典印度哲学整体理解为断然否认。
locator: SEP Buddha：'the Buddha never categorically denies the existence of a self that transcends what is empirically given, namely the five skandhas or psychophysical elements'（引 Albahari 2006 为例）；'all of classical Indian philosophy—Buddhist and orthodox alike—understood the Buddha to have denied the self tout court'
note: packet 按来源并陈，不采边。

claim: 涅槃=贪瞋痴的吹熄/熄灭、轮回再生的永久止息；'不是东西而是事件或经验'；早期文本少谈其形而上性质。
locator: Wikipedia Pre-sectarian Buddhism Nirvana 节：'means the 'blowing out' or 'extinguishing' of greed, aversion, and delusion (the simile used in texts is that of a flame going out), and that this signifies the permanent cessation of samsara and rebirth'；Gethin：'this is not a 'thing' but an event or experience'；Kasulis：'there is little discussion in the early Buddhist texts about the metaphysical nature of nirvana, since they seem to hold that metaphysical speculation is an obstacle to the goal'（内层引号字形从原文）
note: 结论部分亦用此条。

claim: Vetter 的修行论最小核心说：经文最初可能只以中道为核心、中道指向禅那；佛陀最初寻求'不死'。
locator: Wikipedia Pre-sectarian Buddhism Teachings 段：'Originally the text may only have pointed at the Middle Way as being the core of the Buddha's teaching,'与'which pointed to the practice of dhyana.'（两句间原文有脚注100，分引）；'itself a condensation of a longer sequence'；'the Four Truths were then added as a description of the Buddha's 'liberating insight''；'the Buddha at first sought 'the deathless' (amata/amrta), which is concerned with the here and now.'（内层引号字形从原文）
note: Vetter 专著（BRILL 1988）未直接核读，按 S3 转述层呈现并已在 evidenceLimits 声明；书名/出版社/年份经 S3 参考文献核验：'last: Vetter first: Tilmann year: 1988 title: The Ideas and Meditative Practices of Early Buddhism publisher: BRILL'。
uncertainty: 专著原文未核读，全部经由 S3 转述。

claim: 口传机制：教说身后不久复诵、经口传保存至书写；结集（saṅgīti）本义'共同诵出/合诵'。
locator: SEP Buddha：'the Buddha's discourses were probably rehearsed shortly after his death and preserved through oral transmission until the time they were committed to writing'；Wikipedia First Buddhist council：'saṅgīti, literally meaning "reciting together" or "joint rehearsal"'（内层引号字形从原文双引号）

claim: 文本传递被部派争议塑造（插入与删除）。
locator: SEP Buddha：'it suggests textual transmission involved processes of insertion and deletion in aid of one side or another in sectarian disputes.'
note: conclusion 第一段直接引用。

claim: 巴利藏书面化：前29—17年斯里兰卡阿卢寺；传统说距佛灭约454年；'佛说'系非字面意义；口诵传统长期并行；巴利语非摩揭陀语。
locator: Wikipedia Pali Canon：'The Theravādin pitakas were first written down in Sri Lanka in the Alu Viharaya Temple no earlier than 29–17 BC.'；'written down on palm leaves during the Fourth Buddhist Council in 29 BC, approximately 454 years after the death of Gautama Buddha'；'The claim that the texts were "spoken by the Buddha" is meant in this non-literal sense.'；'The existence of the Bhāṇaka tradition existing until later periods, along with other sources, shows that oral tradition continued to exist side by side with written scriptures for many centuries to come.'；'linguists have identified Pali as being more closely related to other prakrit languages of western India'

claim: 重构诸立场：Schmithausen 三立场；Lamotte 基本一致说；中村元无一词可确考说及最早层判断；Vetter 约前270上限；Conze/Warder 两部共有标准；'core within this core'。

claim: 四谛分层争议双方：Norman '圣'字后加、Schmithausen 四谛较晚、Anderson 从律入经 vs Anālayo 平行本一致支持传统说法。
locator: Wikipedia Pre-sectarian Buddhism：'K. R. Norman concluded that the earliest version of the Dhammacakkappavattana Sutta did not contain the word "noble", but was added later.'；'Lambert Schmithausen concluded that the four truths were a later development in early Buddhism.'；'the four noble truths were probably not part of the earliest strata of what came to be recognized as Buddhism, but that they emerged as a central teaching in a slightly later period that still preceded the final redactions of the various Buddhist canons.'（Anderson）；'The Four Truths probably entered the Sutta Pitaka from the Vinaya, the rules for monastic order.'；Wikipedia Dhammacakkappavattana Sutta（Anālayo）：'there is no compelling basis for questioning the traditional account that the four truths were the topic of the Buddha's first sermon' 与 'What remains uncertain, however, is how far these four truths were from the outset qualified as "noble."'
